stem: What do local shape descriptors (LSDs) encode about the neuron under each voxel?
choices: The neuron's global identity across the whole volume
Local statistics such as diameter, elongation and direction
Distances to the nearest synapse and organelle
Membrane probabilities at several image scales
answer: Local statistics such as diameter, elongation and direction
label: Abstract · what LSDs capture

stem: Which three statistics of the object under a voxel, aggregated over a local Gaussian window, make up a local shape descriptor?
choices: Surface area, curvature and boundary distance
Intensity mean, variance and gradient direction
Volume, voxel-relative centre of mass and coordinate correlations
Volume, skeleton length and branch count
answer: Volume, voxel-relative centre of mass and coordinate correlations
label: Intro · LSD components

stem: How many dimensions does the local shape descriptor embedding predicted per voxel have?
label: Fig 1 · LSD dimensionality

stem: Assuming linear scaling on 1,000 contemporary GPUs, how long would flood-filling networks take to process a complete mouse brain?
choices: About 226 years
About 2.3 years
About 22.6 years
About 125 years
answer: About 226 years
label: Intro · FFN mouse-brain cost

stem: How much manual effort would it take to trace each of the estimated 100,000 neurons of a Drosophila brain to completion?
choices: About 226 years
About 125 years
About 12 years
About 1,250 years
answer: About 125 years
label: Intro · manual fly tracing

stem: How does the ACRLSD architecture differ from ACLSD?
choices: Its second network also receives the raw EM data
It predicts LSDs and affinities in a single pass
It adds long-range affinity neighbours
It trains the second network with MALIS loss
answer: Its second network also receives the raw EM data
label: Results · ACRLSD vs ACLSD

stem: What does the multitask LSD network (MTLSD) predict?
choices: LSDs first, then affinities from them in a second network
LSDs and direct-neighbour affinities in a single pass
Affinities with three extra neighbours per direction
A single object mask grown from a seed
answer: LSDs and direct-neighbour affinities in a single pass
label: Results · MTLSD design

stem: Which three large data sets were used to benchmark LSD-based segmentation against other methods?
choices: ZEBRAFINCH, FAFB and MICrONS
CREMI, SNEMI3D and FIB-25
ZEBRAFINCH, HEMI-BRAIN and FIB-25
HEMI-BRAIN, FAFB and H01
answer: ZEBRAFINCH, HEMI-BRAIN and FIB-25
label: Results · benchmark data sets

stem: What does the min-cut metric (MCM) proposed in the LSD paper measure?
choices: Information lost between segmentation and ground truth
Expected error-free path length along skeletons
Voxel-wise boundary disagreement with ground truth
Graph edit operations needed in a hypothetical proofreading tool
answer: Graph edit operations needed in a hypothetical proofreading tool
label: Results · min-cut metric

stem: Which common assumption behind segmentation metrics do the authors note next-generation proofreading tools challenge?
choices: False merges take much longer to fix than false splits
False splits take much longer to fix than false merges
Merges and splits take equal time to fix
Errors in small objects take longest to fix
answer: False merges take much longer to fix than false splits
label: Results · merge vs split cost

stem: On the ZEBRAFINCH data set, how did LSD-based networks compare with the other affinity-based methods across ROI sizes?
choices: Better only on the smallest ROIs
Consistently better across the range of ROIs
Better only on the full BENCHMARK ROI
Indistinguishable within noise
answer: Consistently better across the range of ROIs
label: Results · LSD vs affinities

stem: On ZEBRAFINCH, how did the best auto-context LSD network (ACRLSD) compare with flood-filling networks by variation of information?
choices: Far worse than FFN
Far better than FFN
On par with FFN
Better than FFN only without masking
answer: On par with FFN
label: Results · ACRLSD vs FFN accuracy

stem: What did the ZEBRAFINCH experiments show about method rankings measured on small evaluation ROIs (up to 54 µm)?
choices: They predicted large-volume rankings well
They favoured FFN over every affinity method
They matched rankings by min-cut metric only
They did not extrapolate to larger volumes
answer: They did not extrapolate to larger volumes
label: Results · small ROIs mislead

stem: Why does expected run length (ERL) behave erratically when skeletons are cropped to smaller ROIs?
choices: Shorter skeleton fragments lower ERL even without errors
Cropping removes the merge errors ERL depends on
ERL rises with every additional skeleton
Cropping introduces false splits at ROI borders
answer: Shorter skeleton fragments lower ERL even without errors
label: Results · ERL and fragments

stem: To which error type is the expected run length metric disproportionately sensitive?
choices: Split errors
Merge errors
Boundary-placement errors
Missed small fragments
answer: Merge errors
label: Results · ERL merge sensitivity

stem: On the ZEBRAFINCH BENCHMARK ROI, how did ACRLSD compare with FFN on VOI?
choices: Higher total VOI but a lower merge component
Lower total VOI and a lower merge component
Lower total VOI but a higher merge component
Higher total VOI and a higher merge component
answer: Lower total VOI but a higher merge component
label: Results · VOI split

stem: What expected run lengths did ACRLSD and FFN reach on the ZEBRAFINCH BENCHMARK ROI?
choices: 16.7 µm for ACRLSD, 13.5 µm for FFN
13.5 mm for ACRLSD, 16.7 mm for FFN
2.2 µm for ACRLSD, 2.3 µm for FFN
13.5 µm for ACRLSD, 16.7 µm for FFN
answer: 13.5 µm for ACRLSD, 16.7 µm for FFN
label: Results · ERL values

stem: How did the min-cut metric scale with evaluation ROI size?
choices: Linearly
Erratically, like ERL
Quadratically
It stayed roughly constant
answer: Linearly
label: Results · MCM scaling

stem: Given that the min-cut metric approximates proofreading effort, which existing metric do the authors recommend for comparing segmentations in a min-cut proofreading workflow?
choices: Expected run length, since it mostly agrees with MCM
Variation of information, since it mostly agrees with MCM
Adapted Rand error, since it mostly agrees with MCM
Neither, since both disagree with MCM
answer: Variation of information, since it mostly agrees with MCM
label: Results · VOI recommended

stem: What happened to segmentation accuracy when large ZEBRAFINCH ROIs were processed without a neuropil mask?
choices: It degraded only for FFN
It was essentially unchanged
It degraded substantially for every method
It improved because glia were segmented too
answer: It degraded substantially for every method
label: Results · masking

stem: In the extended experiment on small ssTEM volumes of mouse visual cortex, when did LSD networks outperform baselines most noticeably?
choices: In the multitask setup
With MALIS loss
With long-range affinities
In an auto-context setup
answer: In an auto-context setup
label: Results · mouse ssTEM

stem: How does adding LSD prediction change computational cost relative to baseline direct-neighbour affinity networks?
choices: Almost no difference
About twofold higher
About tenfold higher
About a hundredfold higher
answer: Almost no difference
label: Results · LSD overhead

stem: How much more computationally efficient (in FLOPs) is ACRLSD than flood-filling networks at comparable segmentation quality?
choices: About fivefold
About two orders of magnitude
About one order of magnitude
About four orders of magnitude
answer: About two orders of magnitude
label: Results · efficiency vs FFN

stem: Why did the authors restrict their FLOP comparison to GPU operations?
choices: CPU agglomeration was identical across methods
FFN reported only GPU numbers
CPU FLOP estimates are unreliable and GPU work dominates
CPU work was parallelised away by block-wise processing
answer: CPU FLOP estimates are unreliable and GPU work dominates
label: Results · GPU-only FLOPs

stem: By what factor can a coarse-to-fine, multi-scale approach improve flood-filling network throughput?
choices: About two
About twenty
About a hundred
About five
answer: About five
label: Results · FFN coarse-to-fine

stem: Why do the authors think LSDs help as an auxiliary task for boundary prediction?
choices: They force use of more of the receptive field than boundaries need
They double the amount of labelled training data
They let the network ignore plasma membranes
They make the loss landscape convex
answer: They force use of more of the receptive field than boundaries need
label: Discussion · why LSDs help

stem: What did an auto-context baseline (affinities fed into a second affinity network, ACBASELINE) achieve over the plain baseline?
choices: An improvement matching ACLSD
No substantial improvement
A small improvement on large ROIs only
Worse accuracy from overfitting
answer: No substantial improvement
label: Discussion · ACBASELINE

stem: What do the authors suspect the second network of an affinities-from-affinities cascade does?
choices: Overfits to the training volumes
Learns long-range context the first pass missed
Copies its input rather than learning anything new
Learns to predict LSDs implicitly
answer: Copies its input rather than learning anything new
label: Discussion · copying hypothesis

stem: How does the combined volume of the three CREMI challenge test sets compare with the smallest ZEBRAFINCH evaluation ROI?
choices: About ten times larger
About the same as the full BENCHMARK ROI
About twice as large
It is smaller
answer: It is smaller
label: Discussion · challenge test size

stem: How many manually ground-truthed test skeletons were used to evaluate segmentations on the ZEBRAFINCH data set?
label: Results · test skeletons
